issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Milkable.messageOnMilk() to be a no-argument method returning a String (per UML and usage in template Main), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) with a double parameter. This parameter mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from compiling or following the provided template Main code which calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable.messageOnMilk method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to implement messageOnMilk() with no parameters and return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (remove the double parameter and associated volume usage), or (B) update the problem statement and template Main to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and adjust instructions/examples to include the volume parameter. Preferred fix: align solution to the original specification by removing the double parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a parameterless Milkable.messageOnMilk() (returns a String like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), but the solution's Milkable interface and its implementations use messageOnMilk(double volume). This signature mismatch (same conceptual method with different parameters) breaks the direct mapping between the exercise description/template and the reference implementation and will confuse students (and cause compilation or runtime mismatches).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable.messageOnMilk method signature consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to declare messageOnMilk() without parameters (String messageOnMilk()), and update Seal and Goat to implement this parameterless version returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if volume is required, update the problem statement and template to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and show the expected return format accordingly.
